title: Foundations of Health Care: Safe Sleep, Nutrition, and Play
summary: Foundations of care in the first months: Sleeping on the back to reduce the risk of sudden infant death, breastfeeding or formula feeding on demand while monitoring signs of hunger and fullness (lip-smacking, head-turning, swallowing), and avoiding screens entirely under the age of two—children learn through talking, playing, and sensory exploration. Every waking moment is an opportunity for growth: hold your child, stay close, and describe what you are doing aloud.
try_this: This week: A consistent sleep routine—warm bath, gentle massage, a short story or Qur’anic verse, then bed while drowsy but still awake. And watch for hunger signs before crying: mouth movements, hand-sucking, restlessness.
reflection_prompts: What was the most difficult challenge you faced in the sleep routine? How did you handle it?
Have you noticed a difference in your child’s response when you describe what you are doing during care?
